57     private fun refusal(r: NodeResult<*>, what: String): Exception = when (r) {
58         is NodeResult.Refused -> if (r.code == "PROOF_BACKEND_UNAVAILABLE") PartNotConfigured("Not configured on the node: ${NodeAgentProtocol.explain(r.code)}")
!!                                                                                               ^ error
59             else IllegalStateException("$what refused: ${r.message}")
60         is NodeResult.Unreachable -> IllegalStateException("Node unreachable during $what: ${r.message}")
61         is NodeResult.Ok -> IllegalStateException("unexpected")

66         assertEquals(State.NOT_READ, ReadingFreshness.state(null, 10_000, lastReadFailed = false))
67         assertEquals(State.FRESH, ReadingFreshness.state(10_000, 10_000 + ReadingFreshness.STALE_AFTER_MS, lastReadFailed = false))
68         assertEquals(State.STALE, ReadingFreshness.state(10_000, 10_001 + ReadingFreshness.STALE_AFTER_MS, lastReadFailed = false))
!!                                                                  ^ error
69         assertEquals(State.LAST_READ_FAILED, ReadingFreshness.state(10_000, 10_500, lastReadFailed = true))
70         // Monotonic time going backwards (e.g. a reading from another boot) is never presented as fresh.
71         assertEquals(State.STALE, ReadingFreshness.state(10_000, 5_000, lastReadFailed = false))

### style, MagicNumber (393)

Report magic numbers. Magic number is a numeric literal that is not defined as a constant and hence it's unclear what the purpose of this number is. It's better to declare such numbers as constants and give them a proper name. By default, -1, 0, 1, and 2 are not considered to be magic numbers.

[Documentation](https://detekt.dev/docs/rules/style#magicnumber)
